generations.raw_text: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-associated degradation (ERAD) is a principal mechanism that targets ER-associated proteins for cytosolic proteasomal degradation. Here, our data demonstrate a critical role for the Sel1L-Hrd1 complex in maintaining an early checkpoint in B cell development. Our results show that a mutation in the *Sel1L* gene, which encodes a component of the Sel1L-Hrd1 ERAD complex, causes the death of pro-B cells and prevents them from progressing to pre-B cells. We also found that this mutation leads to upregulation of several important early B cell genes, suggesting that this complex acts as a key negative regulator to control the expression of these early B cell genes. Together, these results indicate that the Sel1L-Hrd1 complex plays a key role in the negative regulation of the expression of some important early B cell genes and the positive regulation of the expression of some important late B cell genes, acting as a check point at the early B cell stage.
